name: Johanna Ferrour
description: Named in post-revolt indictment records as a leading participant in the London violence, including accusations of involvement in the killing of Richard Lyons and the burning of the Savoy Palace. One of the very few women named individually in the revolt's court records. No evidence survives of her being executed or punished as severely as male leaders were, which historians note without being able to fully explain from the surviving record.
narrative_function: The clearest documented instance of a woman in a leadership-level role in the London violence -- and a genuine gap in what the punishment record can tell us.
